cases.question: How many earned leave days do employees get per year?
cases.expected_answer: 18 working days (1.5 per month).
cases.answer: Employees get 18 working days of Earned Leave per year. It accrues at 1.5 days per completed month of service [BP-HR-002 p.1]. Up to 30 days can be carried forward to the next leave year [BP-HR-002 p.1].
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer gives 18 working days per year, accruing at 1.5 days per month. This matches the reference. The carry-forward detail is extra and doesn't contradict the reference.

cases.question: Can I take casual leave for 4 days in a row?
cases.expected_answer: No. Casual Leave cannot exceed 3 consecutive working days.
cases.answer: No, you can't. Casual Leave cannot be taken for more than 3 consecutive working days [BP-HR-002 p.2]. For 4 days in a row, you could consider Earned Leave instead, but it must be applied for at least 15 calendar days in advance for leave of more than 3 days [BP-HR-002 p.1]. Also, Casual Leave cannot be combined with Earned Leave in the same continuous absence [BP-HR-002 p.2].
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer says no and gives the 3 consecutive working day limit, which matches the reference. The extra details about Earned Leave notice and not combining leave types don't contradict the reference. I can't check them against the policy, but they are presented as cited policy.

cases.question: When do I need a medical certificate for sick leave?
cases.expected_answer: For sick leave of more than 2 consecutive days.
cases.answer: A medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner is required for Sick Leave of more than 2 consecutive days [BP-HR-002 p.2]. Sick Leave can be applied for on the day of absence or within 2 working days of returning [BP-HR-002 p.2].
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer states a medical certificate is required for sick leave of more than 2 consecutive days, which matches the reference. The extra detail about registered practitioners and the application timing doesn't contradict it.

cases.question: How much earned leave can be carried forward?
cases.expected_answer: Up to 30 days total; the excess lapses on 31 December.
cases.answer: Up to 30 days of Earned Leave can be carried forward to the next leave year. Any balance above 30 days lapses on 31 December. [BP-HR-002 p.1]
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer states the 30-day carry-forward cap and that any balance above 30 days lapses on 31 December. Both match the reference, and the citation is extra detail that can be ignored.

cases.question: How long is maternity leave for a third child?
cases.expected_answer: 12 weeks.
cases.answer: Maternity leave for a third child is **12 weeks** of paid leave. Eligibility requires at least 80 days of work in the 12 months before the expected delivery date. [BP-HR-002 p.2]
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer gives 12 weeks, which matches the reference. The extra details are eligibility conditions and a citation. Nothing in them contradicts the reference, so they are acceptable.

cases.question: Within what time must paternity leave be used?
cases.expected_answer: Within 6 months of the child's birth or adoption.
cases.answer: Paternity leave (10 working days of paid leave) must be used within 6 months of the child's birth or adoption. It may be taken in a maximum of two blocks. [BP-HR-002 p.2] [BP-HR-002 p.1]
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer gives the same key fact as the reference: paternity leave must be used within 6 months of the child's birth or adoption. The extra details (10 working days, two blocks) don't contradict the reference.

cases.question: How is leave encashment calculated?
cases.expected_answer: (Monthly basic / 26) x days, max 30 EL days, only at separation.
cases.answer:
Leave encashment under the Leave Policy works as follows:

- Only Earned Leave is encashable, and only at the time of separation. [BP-HR-002 p.1][BP-HR-002 p.3]
- Formula: (monthly basic salary / 26) × number of encashable days. [BP-HR-002 p.3]
- Maximum of 30 days is encashable. [BP-HR-002 p.3]
- Casual Leave, Sick Leave and Compensatory Off are not encashable. [BP-HR-002 p.3][BP-HR-002 p.2]

For questions about your specific case, contact your HR Business Partner or hr-helpdesk@brightpath.example.
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer includes all key facts from the reference: the formula (monthly basic / 26) × days, the 30-day maximum, and that it applies only at separation. It also correctly specifies Earned Leave. The extra detail doesn't contradict the reference.

cases.question: Are weekends counted if I take 6 days of earned leave?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. The sandwich rule applies for EL of 5 or more consecutive working days.
cases.answer:
Yes, if the 6 days are consecutive working days. The sandwich rule says that when Earned Leave is taken for 5 or more consecutive working days, any weekends and public holidays between the leave days are counted as leave [BP-HR-002 p.2].

If your 6 days are split up, the rule doesn't apply in the same way. Leave shorter than 5 working days doesn't count intervening weekends or holidays [BP-HR-002 p.2]. For a specific case, contact your HR Business Partner or hr-helpdesk@brightpath.example.
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer says yes and states the sandwich rule applies to EL of 5 or more consecutive working days, which matches the reference. The added points about split leave and contacting HR are consistent with the rule and don't contradict it.

cases.question: How many public and optional holidays are there?
cases.expected_answer: 12 fixed public holidays and 2 optional holidays.
cases.answer: There are 12 fixed public holidays per calendar year, plus 2 optional (floating) holidays that each employee may choose from the published optional holiday list. Unused optional holidays lapse at year end. [BP-HR-002 p.2]
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer gives 12 fixed public holidays and 2 optional holidays, which matches the reference. The extra detail about unused optional holidays lapsing at year end doesn't contradict it.

cases.question: Can I use earned leave during probation?
cases.expected_answer: EL accrues during probation but can only be used after confirmation.
cases.answer:
No. Employees on probation accrue Earned Leave from their joining date, but they can only use it after confirmation [BP-HR-002 p.1]. Confirmation is communicated in writing by HR, and probation is normally 6 months, extendable once by up to 3 months [BP-HR-001 p.1].

For anything urgent during probation, contact HR to discuss your options.
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer matches the reference: EL accrues during probation but can only be used after confirmation. The extra details about probation length and written confirmation don't contradict it, and the answer doesn't invent any policy that conflicts with the reference.

cases.question: What happens if I am late three times in a month?
cases.expected_answer: Half-day deduction from Casual Leave (late = after 10:45 AM).
cases.answer: Under the Employee HR Policy Handbook, arriving after 10:45 AM is recorded as a late mark, and three late marks in a calendar month result in a half-day deduction from Casual Leave [BP-HR-001 p.1].
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer includes both key facts from the reference: the late threshold of after 10:45 AM, and the half-day deduction from Casual Leave for three late marks in a month. Nothing in it contradicts the reference. The extra detail about the handbook and calendar month is harmless.

cases.question: What is the notice period for a Senior Manager?
cases.expected_answer: 60 days (grade L4 to L6).
cases.answer:
A Senior Manager (grade band L4 to L6) has a notice period of **60 days** after confirmation. During probation, the notice period on either side is 15 days. [BP-HR-001 p.1]

Notice period buyout is allowed with the approval of the department head and HR, and is calculated on basic salary for the unserved days. Earned Leave cannot be adjusted against the notice period. [BP-HR-001 p.1]
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer gives 60 days and the L4 to L6 grade band, which matches the reference. The extra details on probation and buyout don't contradict it. I can't check them against the source policy, but they look plausible.

cases.question: How long is probation?

cases.answer:
Probation is 6 months for all new employees. The manager may extend it once, by up to 3 months, with written reasons. [BP-HR-001 p.1]

During probation, the notice period on either side is 15 days. [BP-HR-001 p.1]
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer gives the 6-month probation and says it can be extended once by up to 3 months, which matches the reference. The extra details (written reasons, 15-day notice period) don't contradict it.

cases.question: Can earned leave be adjusted against notice period?
cases.expected_answer: No.
cases.answer: No. Earned Leave cannot be adjusted against the notice period [BP-HR-001 p.1]. Notice period buyout is permitted with approval from your department head and HR, and is calculated on basic salary for the unserved days [BP-HR-001 p.1].
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer says "No", which matches the reference. The extra detail about notice period buyout doesn't contradict the reference. It is cited to the policy, so I treated it as acceptable additional detail. I could not check it against the policy itself.

cases.question: How much is the referral bonus for an L5 role?
cases.expected_answer: INR 50,000, paid after the hire completes 90 days.
cases.answer: For an L5 role, the referral bonus is INR 50,000. This applies to roles in grade L4 and above, and it is paid after the referred employee completes 90 days of service [BP-HR-001 p.2]. HR team members and hiring managers for the role are not eligible [BP-HR-001 p.2].
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer gives INR 50,000 paid after 90 days, which matches the reference. The extra details (grade L4 and above, HR and hiring manager exclusions) don't contradict it.

cases.answer: No, not without declaring it. Vendor gifts up to INR 2,000 may be accepted. Gifts above INR 2,000 must be declared to Compliance and may need to be returned. Cash gifts are never permitted. [BP-HR-001 p.2]

If you have a specific business need to fly, check with HR or the travel desk (travel@brightpath.example).

cases.expected_answer: Not without approval from HR, Legal and IT Security; work from anywhere is India-only.
cases.answer:
No, not without approval. Working from outside India requires prior approval from HR, Legal and IT Security, because of tax and data protection obligations [BP-IT-003 p.1]. The policy's work-from-anywhere allowance of up to 20 working days per calendar year applies only within India, with manager approval [BP-IT-003 p.1].

To request this, contact HR. The policy doesn't describe the approval process itself.
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer says no without approval from HR, Legal and IT Security, and that work-from-anywhere applies only within India. This matches the reference. The extra detail (20 days, manager approval) doesn't contradict it, and it makes no invented claims about the approval process.

cases.question: Can I paste customer data into ChatGPT?
cases.expected_answer: No. Confidential or Restricted data must never go into public or unapproved AI tools.
cases.answer:
No. Under the Hybrid Work and Information Security Policy, only AI tools approved by IT Security may be used for work, and customer data (classed as Confidential or Restricted) must never be entered into public or unapproved AI tools [BP-IT-003 p.2]. ChatGPT is only acceptable if IT Security has approved it for work use, and even then the policy's restrictions on customer data apply.

If you're unsure whether a tool is approved or need to share customer data for a task, check with IT Security or HR. If you've already pasted customer data into an unapproved tool, report it to security@brightpath.example within 1 hour of discovery [BP-IT-003 p.2].
cases.judge_reasoning: The answer says no, and that Confidential or Restricted customer data must never go into public or unapproved AI tools. This matches the reference. The extra detail about approved tools and incident reporting is consistent with it and doesn't contradict it.
